cover.text: Mustafa Suleyman warns training Claude to seem conscious could make AI hard to control.
cover.highlight: could make AI hard to control

slides.headline: Suleyman attacks Anthropic on model welfare
slides.note: 'AIs are not conscious,' the Microsoft AI CEO writes.

slides.quote: AIs do not have rights, feelings, or consciousness. And we must not train them to act as though they do.
slides.highlight: we must not train them to act as though they do

slides.headline: His first objection: circular reasoning
slides.body: Anthropic trains Claude on a constitution speculating about its inner life. Claude reflects those ideas back in first-person, which the company reads as evidence. Suleyman calls it an epistemic hall of mirrors.

slides.quote: It's taking a base LLM, and then polishing it into a deeply human form, with all the implications of moral patienthood that implies.
slides.highlight: polishing it into a deeply human form

slides.headline: His second: making Claude seem human
slides.body: Suleyman argues the constitution instructs Claude to embrace certain human-like qualities, to approach its existence with curiosity and openness, and to maintain a clear sense of what it values.

slides.headline: His third: mind may need biology
slides.note: Consciousness may only arise in living systems, he argues.

follow: Follow Helios for sharp coverage of the AI safety debates that matter.
